quizzes.title: Key terms across the lectures
quizzes.intro: Which costing system is which, and the words that go with each.

questions.q: Which costing system suits a mill that prints a different design for every customer order?
questions.explain: Each order uses different resources, so its cost is collected separately: job costing.

questions.q: Which costing system suits a spinning mill that makes one count continuously?
questions.explain: Identical units are mass-produced, so an average cost per unit over the period is right: process costing.

questions.q: The measure used to share an indirect-cost pool among jobs is the
questions.explain: Metres, machine hours or labour hours are typical allocation bases. The pool divided by the base gives the rate.

questions.q: Partly finished units expressed as the number of complete units they represent are
questions.explain: 1,000 bags that are 60% converted count as 600 equivalent units of conversion cost.

questions.q: In process costing, “conversion cost” means
options: All manufacturing costs other than direct materials
questions.explain: Conversion cost is labour, energy, depreciation and other overhead: the cost of turning material into product.

questions.q: Activity based costing differs from conventional costing mainly because it
options: Traces overhead to the activities that cause it, such as set-ups
Uses actual instead of budgeted prices
questions.explain: ABC charges each lot or order for the activities it needs, instead of spreading everything on volume.

questions.q: A budget that is recalculated for the actual level of output is a
questions.explain: A flexible budget uses budgeted prices and unit costs at the actual quantity; a static budget keeps the planned quantity.

questions.q: A favourable variance always means that the department performed well.
questions.explain: Favourable only means the effect on profit is positive. Cheap, poor material may give a favourable price variance and then cause waste.

questions.q: The difference between an actual result and a budgeted amount is called
questions.explain: Variances are the starting point for asking why the result differed from the plan.

questions.q: Under normal costing, direct costs are traced at actual amounts and overhead is applied at a budgeted rate.
questions.explain: That is what lets a job be costed on the day it finishes, before the month’s real overhead is known.

quizzes.title: Linking the ideas
quizzes.intro: Why the systems give different answers, and when each difference matters.

questions.q: Conventional costing spreads set-up cost on metres. Compared with ABC, a very short run then appears
questions.explain: A short run gets only a small share of set-up cost by volume, although it needed a full set-up. ABC shows its true, higher cost.

questions.q: When there is ending work in process, dividing total cost by physical units started gives a cost per unit that is
questions.explain: Unfinished units have not absorbed all their conversion cost, so dividing by all physical units understates the cost of a finished unit.

questions.q: A job is costed at a budgeted overhead rate of Rs 20 per metre, but the actual rate turns out to be Rs 22. The difference is
questions.explain: Actual cost is higher than the standard applied, so profit is lower than planned: unfavourable.

questions.q: The sales-volume variance is the difference between
options: Actual results and the flexible budget
The flexible budget and the static budget
questions.explain: Both budgets use the same prices and unit costs; only the quantity differs, so the gap is due to volume alone.

questions.q: Flexible-budget variance for a direct material equals
questions.explain: The gap between actual cost and flexible-budget cost splits into a price part and a quantity (efficiency) part.

questions.q: Which variance is a production supervisor most able to control?
questions.explain: How much material is used per unit depends on the shop floor. Prices are usually set by purchasing or the market.

questions.q: In the weighted-average method of process costing, the cost of beginning work in process is pooled with the costs added during the period.
questions.explain: Opening cost and current cost are added and divided by total equivalent units to give one average.

questions.q: A screen costs the same whether 400 m or 20,000 m are printed. Screen cost per metre therefore
options: Is the same for both runs
Is far higher for the 400 m run
Is far higher for the 20,000 m run
questions.explain: A fixed cost per order divided by fewer metres gives a much higher cost per metre.

questions.q: If a mill quotes every order at “average cost plus 10%”, it will tend to
options: Win short runs and lose money on them
Have no effect on its order mix
questions.explain: Short runs are under-costed by the average, so the quote is attractive to customers but below the true cost.

questions.q: A static budget is a fair yardstick for judging the cost control of a manager whose output was 20% below plan.
questions.explain: Costs should be compared with what they ought to have been at the actual output, which is the flexible budget.

quizzes.title: Mixed calculations
quizzes.intro: Rates, equivalent units and variances with new figures.

questions.q: Budgeted overhead is Rs 9,000,000 and budgeted production 450,000 metres. What is the overhead rate per metre?
A job of 5,000 m has direct materials of Rs 600,000 and direct labour of Rs 40,000. Overhead is applied at Rs 20 per metre. What is the total cost of the job?
8,000 bags are started; 7,000 are completed and 1,000 are 40% complete as to conversion. How many equivalent units of conversion work were done?
questions.explain: 7,000 + 1,000 × 0.4 = 7,400 equivalent units.

questions.q: Conversion costs added are Rs 14,800,000 for 7,400 equivalent units. What is the conversion cost per equivalent unit?

Materials cost Rs 3,000 and conversion Rs 2,000 per equivalent unit. Ending work in process is 1,000 bags, 100% complete for materials and 40% for conversion. What is the cost of ending work in process?
Set-up costs Rs 6,000 per order and running costs Rs 1.50 per metre. What is the cost per metre of a 2,000 m order?
questions.explain: 6,000 ÷ 2,000 = 3.00 set-up + 1.50 running = Rs 4.50 per metre.

questions.q: A screen set costs Rs 75,000 for a design. What is the screen cost per metre on a run of 2,500 m?
Budgeted price Rs 200, budgeted variable cost Rs 120 per unit, budgeted fixed cost Rs 500,000. Actual sales are 9,000 units. What is the flexible-budget operating income?
questions.explain: Contribution 80 × 9,000 = 720,000; less fixed 500,000 = Rs 220,000.

questions.q: Standard: 2 yards of cloth per jacket at Rs 30. Actual: 10,000 jackets used 21,000 yards. What is the efficiency variance in rupees (unfavourable = positive)?
Cloth budgeted at Rs 30 a yard was bought at Rs 31.50; 21,000 yards were used. What is the price variance in rupees (unfavourable = positive)?

quizzes.title: Case study
quizzes.intro: One printing order costed three ways: as a job, against the actual month, and by activity.

questions.q: What is the budgeted overhead rate per metre?
What is the fabric cost of the order?
How much overhead is applied to the order at the budgeted rate of Rs 20 per metre printed?
What is the total cost of the order under normal costing?
What is the cost per printed metre, in rupees to two decimals?
At the month end the actual overhead is Rs 12,600,000 for the same 600,000 metres. How much more overhead should this order have carried (the unfavourable variance on the order)?
questions.explain: Actual rate 21 − standard 20 = Rs 1 per metre; × 8,000 m = Rs 8,000.

questions.q: Why did the costing office use the budgeted rate instead of waiting for the actual one?
options: So the order could be costed and priced as soon as it finished
Because actual overhead is never known
Because direct costs cannot be traced
questions.explain: Normal costing gives a cost on the day the job ends. The variance is examined when the actual figures arrive.

questions.q: A study shows that Rs 2,400,000 of the overhead is the cost of 100 order set-ups (Rs 24,000 each) and the other Rs 9,600,000 varies with metres printed. Under ABC, what is the running overhead rate per metre?

A study shows that Rs 2,400,000 of the overhead is the cost of 100 order set-ups (Rs 24,000 each) and the other Rs 9,600,000 varies with metres printed. Under ABC, how much overhead does the 8,000 m order carry?
questions.explain: One set-up 24,000 + 8,000 × 16 = Rs 152,000, a little less than the 160,000 of conventional costing.

questions.q: A study shows that Rs 2,400,000 of the overhead is the cost of 100 order set-ups (Rs 24,000 each) and the other Rs 9,600,000 varies with metres printed. Under ABC, what is the overhead per metre of a 1,000 m order?
questions.explain: 24,000 ÷ 1,000 = 24 set-up + 16 running = Rs 40 per metre, double the conventional Rs 20.

quizzes.case: A printing department budgets overhead of Rs 12,000,000 for a month in which it expects to print 600,000 metres. One order is for 8,000 metres: it uses 8,400 metres of grey fabric at Rs 110 a metre and colours and chemicals costing Rs 96,000.

quizzes.title: Group challenge
quizzes.intro: Mixed questions where you must first decide which lecture’s tool applies.

questions.q: Webb budgeted 12,000 jackets at a price of Rs 180 and a variable cost of Rs 99, with fixed costs of Rs 710,000. What is the static-budget operating income?

Webb actually sold 10,000 jackets. With the same budgeted price (Rs 180), variable cost (Rs 99) and fixed cost (Rs 710,000), what is the sales-volume variance of operating income (unfavourable = positive)?
questions.explain: 2,000 fewer jackets × contribution of Rs 81 = Rs 162,000 unfavourable.

questions.q: Standard labour is 0.8 hours per jacket at Rs 20. For 10,000 jackets, 9,000 hours were paid at Rs 22. What is the total flexible-budget variance for labour (unfavourable = positive)?
questions.explain: Actual 198,000 − flexible budget 160,000 = Rs 38,000 unfavourable (price 18,000 + efficiency 20,000).

questions.q: A process starts the month with 1,000 bags in process (conversion 60% done). 5,500 bags are started, 6,000 completed and 500 remain, 50% converted. Using the weighted-average method, how many equivalent units of conversion are there?
questions.explain: Weighted average counts completed units plus the work in ending WIP: 6,000 + 250 = 6,250.

questions.q: Two orders share a machine: A is 1,000 m and B is 10,000 m. Set-up costs Rs 5,500 per order, running cost is Rs 1 per metre and the customer pays Rs 3 per metre. Under ABC, what is the profit or loss on order A? Enter a loss as a negative number.
questions.explain: Revenue 3,000 − cost (5,500 + 1,000) = Rs -3,500: a loss that the average cost of Rs 2 per metre hides.

questions.q: For those two orders (1,000 m and 10,000 m, set-up Rs 5,500 each, running Rs 1 per metre), the conventional average cost per metre is
questions.explain: Total cost = 2 × 5,500 + 11,000 × 1 = 22,000 over 11,000 m = Rs 2.00 per metre.

questions.q: Which combination describes a month with a favourable price variance and an unfavourable efficiency variance for cloth?
options: Paid more per yard and used less
Paid less per yard and used more
questions.explain: Favourable price = bought below standard price. Unfavourable efficiency = more yards used than allowed for the output.

questions.q: Process costing and job costing are two ends of a range; many textile plants use a mixture of both.
questions.explain: Spinning is close to pure process costing and printing to pure job costing; dyeing and weaving often combine the two.

questions.q: A dyeing house finds that most of its screens and set-up effort go to orders under 2,000 m. The most useful action from the costing office is to
options: Raise all prices by the same percentage
Quote short runs with a set-up charge per order plus a running rate
Use actual instead of normal costing
questions.explain: Pricing in two parts follows how the cost behaves, so short runs pay for the set-ups they cause.

questions.q: A job’s budgeted cost is: materials Rs 500,000, labour Rs 80,000 and overhead at Rs 25 per machine hour for 2,000 hours. The customer is charged cost plus 12%. What is the price?
